title: Canonical relative section comparison with arbitrary coefficients
statement: For a Grothendieck abelian category A, schemes R,S,T, maps h:T→S, f:S→R, k:T→R with h followed by f equal to k, and an A-valued étale sheaf F on R, construct a natural map on R.Etale from sections of f*F on f-pullbacks to sections of k*F on k-pullbacks. It is the inverse-image unit for h, inverse composition, and restriction along pullback pasting.

source.place: Detailed proof paragraph 2: canonical inverse-image unit maps; categorical composition and pullback-pasting coherence.

proof.text: Whisker the adjunction unit by the opposite base-change functor of f, then whisker the inverse-image composition isomorphism, and finally whisker the opposite pullback-pasting natural transformation by the target presheaf. All three transformations are natural, so their composition is natural. For the composite-unit formula, evaluate the unit compatibility of the inverse-image composition isomorphism, use naturality of its inverse, and cancel the isomorphic pasting restriction. No elements of A are used.

proof_origin.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 2: finite skeleton descent and finite-cochain section continuity; explicit categorical construction with Grothendieck coefficients.

mathlib_searches.query: Inverse image adjunction units commute with composition isomorphisms and pullback pasting for sections of sheaves
The adjunction unit gives a functorial map from sections of an inverse image to sections after another base change and the maps satisfy identity and composition laws

from.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 2: finite skeleton descent and section representatives

lean.statement: def Etale.grothendieckRelativeSectionMap {R S T : Scheme.{u}} (h : T ⟶ S) (f : S ⟶ R) (k : T ⟶ R) (hk : h ≫ f = k) (F : Sheaf R.smallEtaleTopology A) : Etale.grothendieckRelativeSections A f F ⟶ Etale.grothendieckRelativeSections A k F
